test_title: PYST 76: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 25 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: Rohini buys a Bluetooth headphone set for ₹1,700 from a wholesale shop and marks it at ₹2,000. Later on, she allows a discount of 40% on its sale. What is her loss or gain percentage (correct up to two decimal places)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SP = 60% of MP = 0.60 × 2000 = ₹1,200

Loss = CP − SP = 1700 − 1200 = ₹500

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ (500 ÷ 1700) × 100 = 500 ÷ 17 ≈ 29.41%

**∴ The correct answer is 29.41% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹1,700

Marked Price (MP) = ₹2,000

Discount = 40%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − Discount% ÷ 100)

Loss = CP − SP

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f76610b9e825cce48a5d58062c2b86bab7857cea717507f60a9ed70483368940.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ SP = 2000 × (1 − 0.40)

⇒ SP = 2000 × 0.60 = ₹1,200

⇒ Loss = 1700 − 1200 = ₹500

⇒ Loss % = (500 ÷ 1700) × 100

⇒ Loss % = 500 ÷ 17 ≈ 29.41%

**∴ The correct answer is 29.41% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is fundamentally an allowance offered to a buyer, always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Hence, SP = MP − Discount.

Profit & Loss Percentage

Unless otherwise stated, Profit or Loss percentage is strictly calculated with respect to Cost Price (CP). Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Direct Relation between CP and MP

A rapid formula linking CP and MP directly is: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 − Loss%). It bypasses solving for SP.
